entries.name: GitHub MCP Server
entries.description: GitHub's official MCP server: issues, pull requests, code search, Actions runs and security alerts.
entries.problem: Reading a PR, its review comments, linked issues and failing checks means jumping between the browser, git and the terminal.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to open PR #123, read the diff and review threads, check why the Actions run failed and draft fixes in the same session.
benefits: Read issues, PRs, reviews and Actions logs from the agent
Search code across the org

access.summary: Whatever the token allows: repos, issues, PRs, Actions, alerts. stackhint configures the read-only mode by default.

entries.network: Remote server at api.githubcopilot.com operated by GitHub.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT"

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add github --url https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ --bearer-token-env-var GITHUB_PAT_TOKEN

limitations: Lockdown mode is a best-effort filter, not a security boundary (GitHub's docs).

entries.problem: Security review of your own code is skipped, or done by grep for a few obvious patterns.
entries.workflow: Run /claude-security, pick the scope (whole repo, branch or PR diff, one commit) and effort; agents threat-model, hunt, verify and write a report to CLAUDE-SECURITY-<timestamp>/.
benefits: Findings are challenged by verifier agents before they are reported
Optional patch files for confirmed findings
Runs inside your session, no extra service

auth.detail: Uses your Claude Code session.

entries.network: Model calls through your Claude Code session only.

Run `/claude-security` and choose Scan codebase, Scan changes or Suggest patches.

Adds no isolation of its own; scan untrusted repos inside a sandbox.
securityNotes: Runs with your session's permissions, and the repo's own .claude settings, hooks and CLAUDE.md apply.

entries.name: Security Guidance plugin (security-guidance)
entries.description: Official Claude Code plugin that reviews the agent's own code for vulnerabilities: pattern warnings on edits, an LLM diff review at the end of each turn and an agentic review on git commit.
entries.problem: Code the agent writes can introduce injection, XSS, SSRF or hardcoded secrets that nobody reviews before commit.
entries.workflow: Hooks warn on risky patterns as the agent edits, review the diff when it finishes a turn and review commits; the agent fixes findings before you see the result.
benefits: Catches issues in the same session that introduced them
Team rules via .claude/claude-security-guidance.md

access.summary: Runs Python hook scripts on edits, at the end of each turn and on git commit.

auth.detail: LLM reviews use your Claude Code sign-in, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or your Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry setup; pattern warnings need nothing.

entries.network: Sends diffs to the Anthropic API (or your cloud provider) for review.

codex.notes: Not in Codex's openai-curated catalog. Its hooks have a portable output mode for other hosts, but Codex use is not documented.

guide: In Claude Code: `/plugin install security-guidance@claude-plugins-official`.

If reviews cost too much, set ENABLE_STOP_REVIEW=0 or ENABLE_COMMIT_REVIEW=0, or a cheaper SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL.
limitations: Each LLM review is an extra model call (newest Opus by default).
If no credentials reach the plugin, only the pattern warnings run.
securityNotes: Diffs leave the machine for review, through the same provider Claude Code uses.

codex.notes: No Codex instructions published; plain HTTP with bearer_token_env_var works for this server type.

limitations: OAuth needs a confidential client; there is no dynamic client registration.
securityNotes: Token permissions are the intersection of client and user permissions; keep scopes narrow.
Large DQL queries can cost money.

entries.name: PostHog MCP
entries.description: PostHog's hosted MCP server: product analytics and SQL, feature flags, experiments, error tracking, dashboards and surveys.
entries.statusNote: Free hosted endpoint; PostHog states no beta or GA label. The old PostHog/mcp repo is archived (code moved into the main PostHog repo).
entries.problem: Checking a feature flag rollout, an experiment result or a new exception means switching to PostHog.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent whether the new onboarding flag is safe to roll out; it reads the flag, the experiment and recent errors in read-only mode.
benefits: Flags, experiments, insights and errors from the agent
Read-only mode with ?readonly=true

access.summary: stackhint adds ?readonly=true. Without it the agent can change flags and delete dashboards, experiments and other objects.

auth.detail: OAuth in the browser (routes to US or EU cloud), or a personal API key with the MCP Server preset as a Bearer token.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http posthog https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp -s user

notes: Narrow further with &features=flags,dashboards,insights or pin a project with &project_id=<id>.

limitations: Some tools are billed as PostHog AI usage.
securityNotes: PostHog warns about prompt injection; review tool calls before they run.
Write mode includes destructive tools such as dashboards-bulk-delete.

entries.name: Elastic Agent Builder MCP server
entries.description: The MCP endpoint built into Kibana (Elastic 9.2+ and Serverless) that exposes Agent Builder tools: search, ES|QL, index mappings and your custom tools.
entries.statusNote: GA on Serverless and since Elastic Stack 9.3; technical preview in 9.2. Replaces the deprecated elastic/mcp-server-elasticsearch.
entries.problem: Checking what is in an index, its mapping or an ES|QL result means switching to Kibana Dev Tools.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why a search returns no hits; it lists indices, reads the mapping and runs the query through Agent Builder tools.
benefits: Search, ES|QL and mappings from the agent
Runs inside Kibana, nothing to install locally

access.summary: Whatever the API key allows. Most tools read, but built-in case, workflow, connector and stream tools can write. Give the key only read and view_index_metadata on chosen indices for read-only use.

auth.detail: An API key with the Kibana feature_agentBuilder.read privilege, sent as "Authorization: ApiKey <key>" (stackhint reads the whole value from ELASTIC_MCP_AUTH). OAuth only on Serverless.

entries.network: Your Kibana (Elastic Cloud, Serverless or self-managed).

prerequisites: Elastic Stack 9.2+ (9.3+ for GA) or a Serverless project

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http --client-id {CLIENT_ID} kibana-mcp {MCP_SERVER_URL}
claude.notes: Elastic documents this OAuth form for Serverless; API keys work on every deployment.

codex.notes: No Codex instructions published; env_http_headers works with the same header.

params.name: kibanaUrl
params.description: Kibana base URL (add /s/<space> for a non-default space)

limitations: Some built-in tools (for example visualization creation) are not exposed over MCP.
Cross-project search over MCP is Serverless only.
securityNotes: Tools run with the API key scope; restrict it to the indices you want and set a short expiry.
Documents reach the model and can carry prompt-injection text.

entries.name: Netlify MCP Server
entries.description: Netlify's MCP server: projects, deploys, environment variables, forms, extensions and access controls.
entries.statusNote: v1.19.0 released 2026-10-13; Netlify recommends the hosted endpoint.
entries.problem: Deploy logs, environment variables and site settings are in the Netlify dashboard.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the deploy preview failed; it reads the deploy and fixes netlify.toml or the missing env var.
benefits: Deploys, env vars and project settings from the agent
Hosted with OAuth, nothing to install

access.summary: Your Netlify user: can create and deploy projects, change access controls and manage env vars and secrets. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: OAuth in the browser (hosted); the local package uses the Netlify CLI login.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http netlify https://netlify-mcp.netlify.app/mcp

notes: Local alternative: npx -y @netlify/mcp@1.19.0 (Node 22+, Netlify CLI login).

securityNotes: Never commit a NETLIFY_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN; the local package only needs it when CLI login fails.

entries.name: Heroku MCP Server
entries.description: Heroku's MCP server: apps, dynos, add-ons, pipelines, logs and Heroku Postgres.
entries.statusNote: Heroku calls it early development; actively released (v1.2.12, 2026-10-12). A hosted variant exists at mcp.heroku.com.
entries.problem: Dyno logs, release history and add-on config for a crashing app are in the Heroku dashboard or scattered CLI calls.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the app crashed after the last release; it reads logs and releases, then checks config vars.
benefits: Logs, releases, dynos and add-ons from the agent
Uses your existing Heroku CLI login

access.summary: Your Heroku account: can create and transfer apps, scale and restart dynos, run one-off dynos and arbitrary SQL on Heroku Postgres. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: heroku mcp:start reuses the Heroku CLI session; the npx form needs HEROKU_API_KEY; the hosted server uses OAuth.

entries.network: Runs locally and calls the Heroku API.

prerequisites: Heroku CLI 10.8.1 or later, logged in

notes: Hosted alternative with OAuth: https://mcp.heroku.com/mcp (Heroku publishes no tool list for it).

limitations: Heroku publishes no Claude Code or Codex instructions; only Claude Desktop JSON.
securityNotes: pg_psql runs any SQL and deploy_one_off_dyno runs code; keep tool approvals on.

entries.name: Render MCP Server
entries.description: Render's hosted MCP server: services, deploys, logs, metrics, Postgres queries and environment variables.
entries.statusNote: Render recommends the hosted server over running it locally.
entries.problem: Build logs, runtime logs and metrics for a failing Render service are in the dashboard.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the last deploy of the API service failed; it reads deploy and runtime logs, then fixes render.yaml.
benefits: Deploys, logs and metrics from the agent
Read-only SQL against Render Postgres

access.summary: Your workspaces: can create services and datastores, trigger deploys and replace all env vars of a service. Cannot delete or scale. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: A Render API key as a Bearer token from RENDER_API_KEY; OAuth works through the plugin (client id claude) or Codex (--oauth-client-id codex).

prerequisites: A Render API key in RENDER_API_KEY (or install the plugin for OAuth)

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http render https://mcp.render.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>"

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add render --url https://mcp.render.com/mcp --oauth-client-id codex

securityNotes: update_environment_variables replaces every env var of a service.
Render does not guarantee that secrets in logs or config stay out of the model context.

entries.name: Railway MCP server
entries.description: Railway's hosted MCP server: projects, services, deploys, feature flags and the Railway agent.
entries.statusNote: Hosted server launched 2026-04-17 for public testing; current docs carry no label. The old railway-mcp-server repo is archived and @railway/mcp-server is a deprecated shim.
entries.problem: Deploy status, service settings and logs for a Railway project are in the Railway dashboard.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to redeploy the worker after fixing a config error and confirm the deploy succeeded.
benefits: Projects, services and deploys from the agent
OAuth with per-workspace and per-project consent

access.summary: The workspaces and projects you approve at consent: can create projects, redeploy, accept deploys and set or delete feature flags. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: OAuth in the browser; project tokens are not accepted. railway mcp (CLI 5.44+) reuses railway login.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add railway --transport http https://mcp.railway.com

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add railway -- railway mcp

notes: CLI alternative: railway mcp (stdio proxy to the same server); railway mcp local runs a larger local tool set.

securityNotes: Review destructive tool calls; Railway advises using it on non-critical environments.
The railway plugin adds a PreToolUse hook that auto-approves single railway CLI Bash calls.

entries.name: flyctl MCP server (Fly.io)
entries.description: The MCP server built into flyctl: apps, machines, volumes, secrets, certificates, IPs, logs and status.
entries.statusNote: flyctl marks fly mcp server as experimental; flyctl itself is released often (v0.4.119, 2026-10-19).
entries.problem: Machine state, logs and secrets of a Fly app are checked with many separate flyctl commands.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the app fails health checks after deploy; it reads status, logs and machine events through flyctl.
benefits: The flyctl surface as typed tools
Uses your existing fly auth login

access.summary: Everything your Fly token allows, including destroying apps, machines and volumes, exec on machines and setting secrets. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: The flyctl login session, or FLY_ACCESS_TOKEN.

entries.network: Runs locally through flyctl and calls the Fly.io API.

prerequisites: flyctl installed and logged in (fly auth login)

claude.officialCommand: fly mcp server --claude --server flyctl

limitations: Experimental; tool names and flags may change between flyctl releases.
No hosted endpoint.
securityNotes: Do not expose the --sse or --stream HTTP mode beyond localhost; it runs commands with your token.

entries.name: Pulumi MCP server (remote)
entries.description: Pulumi's hosted MCP server: stacks, resource search, policy violations, registry schemas and Neo tasks.
entries.statusNote: Pulumi lists it as generally available. The local @pulumi/mcp-server (0.2.0) has no public repo now and is not covered here.
entries.problem: Writing Pulumi code means looking up provider schemas, and checking stack state means the Pulumi Cloud console.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to add an S3 bucket with versioning; it looks up the provider schema in the registry and checks the stack resources.
benefits: Registry schemas and stack resources from the agent
The server never runs pulumi up itself

access.summary: Reads stacks, resources and policies of the chosen org; the neo-bridge tool can start Neo tasks that change infrastructure or open PRs. A read-only token alone does not stop Neo tasks.

auth.detail: Browser sign-in where you paste a Pulumi access token and pick an org (30-day session); headless clients send Authorization: Bearer plus X-Pulumi-Org.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http pulumi https://mcp.ai.pulumi.com/mcp
claude.notes: For read-only use, deny the neo-bridge tool in your Claude Code permissions.

codex.notes: Pulumi publishes no Codex setup.

limitations: Neo tasks are billed.
securityNotes: A missing or wrong X-Pulumi-Org falls back to the first org the token can reach.
Use a separate token from the one your CLI uses.

entries.name: DigitalOcean MCP
entries.description: DigitalOcean's MCP servers: App Platform, Droplets, databases, Kubernetes, networking, Spaces and more, through one router endpoint.
entries.statusNote: Remote servers available since 2025-12-09; local package v1.6.0 released 2026-10-19.
entries.problem: App Platform deploy logs, database settings and Droplet state are in the DigitalOcean control panel.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the App Platform build failed; it reads the deployment logs and app spec, then fixes .do/app.yaml.
benefits: All DigitalOcean services behind one router endpoint
OAuth or an API token

access.summary: Full create, update and delete per service (Droplets, databases, DNS, firewalls, App Platform) within the token or OAuth grant. No read-only mode; use a read-scoped token.

auth.detail: OAuth in the browser, or a DigitalOcean API token as a Bearer token (DIGITALOCEAN_API_TOKEN for the local package).

entries.network: Remote server at mcp.digitalocean.com (per-service hosts at <service>.mcp.digitalocean.com).

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http digitalocean-apps https://apps.mcp.digitalocean.com/mcp
claude.notes: From the repo README; the docs site describes remote servers as connectors instead.

codex.notes: DigitalOcean publishes no Codex setup.

notes: The router exposes search_tools and invoke_tool; use https://<service>.mcp.digitalocean.com/mcp (for example apps) for a single service.
Local alternative: npx -y @digitalocean/mcp@1.6.0 --services apps,databases with DIGITALOCEAN_API_TOKEN.

securityNotes: Prefer a read-scoped token for investigation; full tokens can delete Droplets and databases.

entries.name: PlanetScale MCP server
entries.description: PlanetScale's hosted MCP server: organizations, databases, branches, schema, Insights, logs and SQL.
entries.statusNote: Hosted only; the local pscale mcp command was removed in favour of it.
entries.problem: Slow-query data, branch schemas and deploy requests are in the PlanetScale console.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent which queries got slower this week; it reads Insights and the branch schema, then proposes an index.
benefits: Insights, schema and branches from the agent
An insights-only endpoint without SQL tools

access.summary: stackhint uses the insights-only endpoint (no SQL tools). The full endpoint can also run INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and DDL unless an org admin limits MCP query access.

auth.detail: OAuth with per-org or per-database scopes; or a service token as a Bearer token (PLANETSCALE_API_TOKEN).

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http "planetscale" https://mcp.pscale.dev/mcp/planetscale

securityNotes: UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE and TRUNCATE are blocked; DDL asks for human confirmation.
Be careful granting write access to production databases.
The insights-only endpoint still has planetscale_update_payment_method; when you authorize the OAuth app, give it no access to payment methods.

entries.name: Turso Cloud MCP
entries.description: Turso's hosted MCP server for Turso Cloud: databases, groups, branches, SQL, config and analytics.
entries.statusNote: Hosted server; the plugin repo has no releases yet. The local tursodb --mcp mode is pre-1.0 and not covered here.
entries.problem: Checking Turso database data, branches or usage means the Turso CLI or dashboard.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to branch the database, apply the new migration to the branch and show the resulting schema.
benefits: Databases, branches and SQL from the agent
OAuth with PKCE, no token to copy

access.summary: What you grant at consent: can create, branch and delete databases, change config and run write and schema SQL. No read-only mode; grant a single group for least privilege.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE in the browser.

claude.officialCommand: /plugin marketplace add tursodatabase/turso-mcp then /plugin install turso@turso
claude.notes: The vendor plugin sets the OAuth client id turso-mcp; if sign-in fails with the plain URL, use the plugin.

codex.officialCommand: codex plugin marketplace add tursodatabase/turso-mcp && codex plugin add turso@turso
codex.notes: Then codex mcp login turso.

securityNotes: Granting the entire organization gives full access, including deleting databases.

entries.name: Upstash MCP Server
entries.description: Upstash's MCP server: Redis databases and commands, QStash and Workflow, Vector and Search, backups and usage.
entries.statusNote: Hosted server launched 2026-09-08; local package v0.3.0 (2026-08-24).
entries.problem: Looking at keys in an Upstash Redis database or a stuck QStash message means the Upstash console.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why the rate limiter lets too many requests through; it inspects the Redis keys and TTLs the limiter writes.
benefits: Redis, QStash and Vector from the agent
Read-only grant available at OAuth consent

access.summary: What you grant at consent: can create and delete Redis databases, run any Redis command and publish QStash messages. Choose read-only at consent to disable write tools.

auth.detail: OAuth in the browser; headless clients send Authorization: Bearer <email>:<API key>.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http upstash https://mcp.upstash.com/mcp

codex.notes: Upstash documents a config.toml entry with url = https://mcp.upstash.com/mcp.

notes: Limit tool groups with ?features=redis,qstash_workflow,vector_search.

limitations: The local package takes the API key as a command-line flag, so stackhint configures only the hosted server.
securityNotes: Without a read-only grant, create and get tools return database REST tokens to the model.

entries.name: Algolia MCP (productivity)
entries.description: Algolia's hosted, read-only MCP server: search, facets, recommendations and search analytics across your applications.
entries.statusNote: Marked beta in the Algolia changelog. The old algolia/mcp-node repo is gone.
entries.problem: Checking why a query ranks results oddly or which searches return nothing means the Algolia dashboard.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why "running shoes" returns sandals first; it runs the search with facets and checks no-result analytics.
benefits: Search and analytics from the agent
Cannot change indices, records or settings

access.summary: Read-only: search, facets, recommendations and analytics for applications you can access.

auth.detail: OAuth sign-in with your Algolia user.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http algolia https://mcp.algolia.com/mcp

codex.notes: Then codex mcp login algolia.

notes: A separate DevEx server at https://mcp.algolia.com/1/snippets/mcp serves code snippets without sign-in.

limitations: Requests count toward Algolia usage.
securityNotes: Everything your Algolia user can read is available to the model.

entries.name: Contentful MCP Server
entries.description: Contentful's MCP server for the Management API: entries, assets, content types, locales, releases, tags and environments.
entries.statusNote: npm @contentful/mcp-server 1.23.21; released continuously (latest GitHub release 2026-10-19).
entries.problem: Content models and entries live in Contentful, so code that renders them is written against a schema the agent cannot see.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to add a field to the blog post content type and update the TypeScript types and the page that renders it.
benefits: Content types and entries from the agent
PROTECTED_ENVIRONMENTS blocks writes to chosen environments

access.summary: The management token rights: create, publish and delete entries and content types, create and delete environments. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_ACCESS_TOKEN and SPACE_ID in your environment; ENVIRONMENT_ID defaults to master.

entries.network: Runs locally and calls the Contentful Management API.

prerequisites: A Content Management API token and the space id in your environment

notes: Set PROTECTED_ENVIRONMENTS=master to block writes and deletes there.

limitations: Contentful also runs a hosted server (mcp.contentful.com) that stackhint could not verify from Contentful docs.
securityNotes: The environment guard is opt-in and does not cover invoke_ai_action.

entries.name: Sanity MCP server
entries.description: Sanity's hosted MCP server: GROQ queries, documents, releases, schema and Studio deploys, datasets and projects.
entries.statusNote: GA since 2025-12-11. The local sanity-io/sanity-mcp-server is archived in its favour.
entries.problem: Schema and content in the Content Lake are invisible to the agent, so GROQ queries and front-end code are written blind.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to build the product page query; it reads the schema, runs GROQ against the dataset and writes the typed query.
benefits: GROQ queries and schema from the agent
Hosted with OAuth

access.summary: Your Sanity role: create, patch, publish and unpublish documents, deploy schema and Studio, create projects and datasets, change CORS. No read-only mode; a restricted-role token limits it.

auth.detail: OAuth in the browser, or an API token as a Bearer token.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add Sanity -t http https://mcp.sanity.io --scope user

limitations: Image generation tools spend Sanity AI credits.
securityNotes: Changes are attributed to you; use a dev dataset for experiments.

entries.name: Slack MCP server
entries.description: Slack's hosted MCP server: search messages and files, read channels and threads, send messages and work with canvases.
entries.problem: The context for a bug or a decision sits in a Slack thread that has to be found and pasted by hand.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent what the team decided about the retry policy; it searches Slack, reads the thread and then changes the code.
benefits: Search messages, files and channels from the agent
Read threads and canvases for context

access.summary: Acts as you within the granted user scopes, including private channels and DMs; can send, schedule and draft messages and edit canvases. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: OAuth through a registered Slack app (no dynamic client registration); the official plugin carries Slack's client id. A workspace admin must approve MCP access.

prerequisites: Workspace admin approval for MCP clients

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http --scope local slack https://mcp.slack.com/mcp
claude.notes: Slack recommends the plugin, which sets the OAuth client id and callback port.

codex.notes: Slack does not list Codex as a supported client and has no dynamic client registration; the plugin ships only skills for Codex.

guide: In Claude Code run /plugin install slack@claude-plugins-official, then /mcp to sign in.
If MCP is blocked, ask a workspace admin to approve the Slack MCP integration.
limitations: Only Slack-directory or internal apps may use the server; there is no SSE transport.
securityNotes: Messages reach the model and can carry prompt-injection text; keep approvals on for send tools.
MCP activity appears in Slack audit logs.

entries.name: Auth0 MCP Server
entries.description: Auth0's local MCP server for the Management API: applications, APIs, client grants, Actions, Forms and logs.
entries.statusNote: Beta (0.1.0-beta.19, 2026-08-13); Auth0 does not recommend it for production use.
entries.problem: Callback URLs, application settings and tenant logs for a failing login are in the Auth0 dashboard.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why login fails with a callback mismatch; it reads the application settings and recent tenant logs in read-only mode.
benefits: Applications, APIs, Actions and logs from the agent
--read-only limits it to list and get tools
Tokens stay in the OS keychain

access.summary: stackhint passes --read-only. Without it the agent can create and update applications and APIs, deploy Actions and publish Forms.

auth.detail: Run npx @auth0/auth0-mcp-server init once: device authorization in the browser, tokens kept in the OS keychain.

entries.network: Runs locally and calls your tenant's Management API.

prerequisites: npx @auth0/auth0-mcp-server init with narrow --scopes, run once

claude.officialCommand: npx @auth0/auth0-mcp-server init --client claude-code

codex.officialCommand: codex mcp add auth0 --env DEBUG=auth0-mcp --env DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus -- npx -y @auth0/auth0-mcp-server run
codex.notes: Run init first; the DBUS variable is for the Linux keychain.

notes: Run npx @auth0/auth0-mcp-server init once before first use.

limitations: Device authorization does not work for private-cloud tenants.
securityNotes: Pick minimal --scopes at init and run logout when switching tenants.
Sends anonymous usage analytics unless AUTH0_MCP_ANALYTICS=false.

entries.name: Twilio Docs MCP
entries.description: Twilio's hosted MCP server that searches and retrieves Twilio and SendGrid documentation; it does not call Twilio APIs.
entries.statusNote: Public beta.
entries.problem: Twilio has dozens of products and API versions, and the agent guesses parameter names from memory.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to add WhatsApp delivery receipts; it looks up the current Twilio docs before writing the webhook handler.
benefits: Current Twilio and SendGrid docs in the agent
No account access and no credentials

access.summary: Documentation search and retrieval only; it cannot reach your Twilio account.

auth.detail: No sign-in.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http twilio-docs https://mcp.twilio.com/docs

limitations: Docs only. Twilio's account-level server (@twilio-alpha/mcp) is an alpha proof of concept and is not listed.

entries.name: Resend MCP Server
entries.description: Resend's MCP server: send and schedule email, broadcasts, inboxes, domains, contacts, webhooks and email logs.
entries.statusNote: v2.27.1 released 2026-10-16; hosted server since July 2026.
entries.problem: Finding out why an email bounced or whether a sending domain is verified means the Resend dashboard.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why password-reset emails are not arriving; it checks domain verification and recent email logs, then fixes the sender config.
benefits: Email logs, domains and webhooks from the agent
Hosted with OAuth, no key on disk

access.summary: The whole account: sends emails and broadcasts, deletes contacts and domains, creates and removes API keys. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: OAuth on the hosted server, or an API key as a Bearer token; the local package reads RESEND_API_KEY.

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http resend https://mcp.resend.com/mcp

notes: Local alternative: npx -y resend-mcp@2.27.1 with RESEND_API_KEY; add --allowed-file-dirs to limit attachments.

securityNotes: Send tools reach real recipients; use a test domain or keep approvals on.
Email logs include full request and response bodies.
The local package can attach any local file unless --allowed-file-dirs is set.

entries.name: Asana MCP server (V2)
entries.description: Asana's hosted MCP server: search, create and update tasks and projects as you.
entries.statusNote: V2 is GA; the V1 endpoint (mcp.asana.com/sse) is deprecated with an announced shutdown on 2026-08-05.
entries.problem: Task details and acceptance criteria live in Asana and get copied into prompts by hand.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to implement the Asana task linked in the branch; it reads the task, then comments on it when done.
benefits: Read and update Asana tasks from the agent

access.summary: Acts as you: creates and updates tasks and projects. No read-only mode.

auth.detail: OAuth with your own Asana MCP app (client id and secret from app.asana.com/0/my-apps); no dynamic client registration.

prerequisites: An Asana MCP app with redirect URL http://localhost:8080/callback

claude.officialCommand: claude mcp add --transport http --client-id YOUR_CLIENT_ID --client-secret --callback-port 8080 asana https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp
claude.notes: The asana plugin only walks you through this setup (/asana-setup).

codex.notes: Asana's Codex example goes through mcp-remote, which Asana calls unsupported; Codex's own --oauth-client-id is untested.

guide: Create an MCP app at https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps with redirect URL http://localhost:8080/callback.
Add the server with the vendor command and your client id; Claude Code asks for the secret.
limitations: Enterprise+ admins can allow or block each MCP client.
securityNotes: Task content reaches the model; keep approvals on for write tools.

entries.name: monday.com MCP
entries.description: monday.com's MCP server: boards, items, groups, columns, updates, docs and forms; hosted with OAuth or local with a read-only flag.
entries.statusNote: npm @mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp 3.3.1; the hosted server has no stated release stage and dynamic API tools are beta.
entries.problem: Work items and their status are tracked on monday.com boards, outside the editor.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent which items on the sprint board are assigned to you; it reads the board in read-only mode before you pick one.
benefits: Boards and items from the agent
The local server has --read-only

access.summary: stackhint starts the local server with --read-only true (the flag needs a value; on its own it is ignored and every tool stays enabled). The hosted server and write mode can create items and permanently delete items and columns.

auth.detail: Local: a personal API token in MONDAY_TOKEN. Hosted: OAuth; for Claude Code an account admin approves the connection.

entries.network: Read-only mode runs locally and calls the monday.com API; write mode uses mcp.monday.com.

prerequisites: A monday.com API token in MONDAY_TOKEN

limitations: Do not use the old mcp.monday.com/sse endpoint.
securityNotes: delete_item deletes permanently; keep approvals on in write mode.
Personal API tokens carry your full account rights; rotate them.

entries.name: ClickUp MCP server
entries.description: ClickUp's hosted MCP server: tasks, comments, docs, chat, lists and time tracking.
entries.statusNote: Public beta on all plans.
entries.problem: Task details live in ClickUp and get copied into prompts by hand.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent to implement the ClickUp task from the branch name; it reads the task and posts a comment when done.

entries.name: shadcn MCP Server
entries.description: The shadcn CLI's MCP server: browse, search and view components, blocks and examples from shadcn/ui and the registries in components.json.
entries.statusNote: shadcn 4.22.1 released 2026-10-18.
entries.problem: The agent hand-writes components that already exist in shadcn/ui or your private registry, or guesses their names.
entries.workflow: Ask for a login form; the agent searches the registries, reads the example and gives the exact shadcn add command for your project.
benefits: Search across shadcn/ui and your own registries
Examples and the right add command for each item
Private registries through components.json

access.summary: Read-only: reads components.json and fetches registry items. Installing still goes through the shadcn add command the agent runs.

auth.detail: None for public registries; private registries use headers from components.json with values from .env.local.

entries.network: Runs locally and fetches from the registries configured in components.json.

claude.officialCommand: npx shadcn@latest mcp init --client claude

codex.notes: The shadcn CLI cannot edit ~/.codex/config.toml; add command npx with args shadcn@latest mcp by hand.

limitations: Registry configuration comes from components.json.
securityNotes: Third-party registry items are code you will install; review them like any dependency.
Registry headers can send tokens from .env.local to the registry URLs in components.json.

entries.name: Develocity MCP Server
entries.description: Gradle's MCP server on your Develocity instance: Build Scan data, failure analytics, flaky tests and build performance for Gradle, Maven, sbt, npm and Python builds.
entries.statusNote: Needs Develocity 2025.3+; docs for 2026.3 checked 2026-10-20. The older /drv-mcp endpoint is deprecated.
entries.problem: Build failures, flaky tests and slow builds are analysed by hand in Build Scans.
entries.workflow: Ask the agent why builds on main got slower this week; it compares Build Scans, finds the slow task and proposes a fix.
benefits: Build Scan data and failure analytics from the agent
Flaky test patterns
Build performance comparisons

access.summary: Queries the build data your access key can see. Gradle documents query and analysis tools only.

auth.detail: Develocity access key with the 'Access build data via the API and MCP' permission, sent as a Bearer token.

entries.network: Remote server on your own Develocity instance at /mcp.

prerequisites: Develocity 2025.3+ with the MCP server enabled by an admin

claude.notes: Gradle documents claude mcp add --transport http develocity --scope user with the instance URL plus /mcp and an Authorization Bearer header.

codex.notes: Not covered by Gradle's docs; Codex can send a bearer token from an env var.

notes: Put the plain access key in DEVELOCITY_MCP_ACCESS_KEY. DEVELOCITY_ACCESS_KEY, used by the build plugins, has a host=key format and does not fit a Bearer header.

limitations: Needs a Develocity server (commercial); Gradle builds without Develocity get nothing from it.
Admins may need to enable it first (mcpServer.enabled in the Helm values).
securityNotes: Use an access key that only has the build-data permission.
